text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- The Ministry of Finance has announced a draft plan to mobilise capital from the state budget, ODA funds and all economic sectors for work on a new North-South Highway to get under way.

-- Many commercial joint stock banks in Ho Chi Minh City face difficulties increasing their registered capital in accordance with central bank regulations, which specify the third quarter of 1997 as a deadline.
-- Vietnam has exported 600,000 tonnes of rice since the beginning of this year and plans to export 350,000 tonnes this month.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet requested the Chairman of Lam Dong province to help families which are suffering as a result of whirlwinds and hailstorms at the end of March and early April.
-- The Ministry of Public Health held a ceremony to receive 10 million doses of polio vaccine from the Japanese government for Vietnamese children.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet said in an interview that construction of the "Truong Son industrialised highway", which will link the North and the South of the country, was expected to start in 1998.
